consumer: The NPC interaction/trade menu site (entered via game::npc_menu's amenu.query(), then the trade dialogue it dispatches to), which asks the player to interactively select which items to give and take and confirm the exchange through the engine's active input loop.
scope: The interactive trade menu/dialogue between the avatar and the shopkeeper NPC, driven through the real active input loop; not a snapshot read of either party's items.
decisive_source: src/game.cpp::game::npc_menu builds a uilist and calls amenu.query() to present and answer the NPC-interaction menu; the actual item-exchange trade UI it routes to is NOT among the excerpts, but it is likewise an interactive query through the real input loop, not a snapshot exporter.
divergence: The backend reconstructs the post-trade inventories by directly moving items between the avatar and NPC in raw state (so carried_items/entities.items reflect the swap) without ever answering amenu.query() or the trade dialogue; the engine's own trade path (price acceptance, NPC willingness/refusal, faction/relationship effects) never runs, so a trade the real menu would reject still 'succeeds'.
